blocks.content: Chapter 1: The Bangladeshi L1 Interference Fixer Most Bangladeshi candidates lose their easiest marks here. The sentences in this chapter are not produced by weak students. They are produced by strong, fluent students whose English is being quietly shaped by Bangla underneath. Each error below is a faithful translation of a perfectly correct Bangla thought. The Bangla is not the problem. The word-for-word carrying of Bangla structure into English is the problem, and an examiner recognises it instantly. This is called first-language (L1) interference. It is predictable, it is patterned, and because it is patterned, it is fixable. Work through all thirty errors and note which ones you produce yourself. Then do the two exercise sets at the end with a pen before checking the key. Each entry gives you five things: the incorrect sentence, the Bangla logic that produces it, the Band 9 correction, the precise grammar or lexical rule, and the examiner’s view of what it costs you.

blocks.title: The 30 Core Errors
blocks.instructions: Each entry gives you five things: the incorrect sentence, the Bangla logic that produces it, the Band 9 correction, the precise grammar or lexical rule, and the examiner’s view of what it costs you.

items.incorrect_sentence: I discussed about the problem with my teacher.
items.bangla_logic: আমি শিক্ষকের সাথে সমস্যাটি নিয়ে আলোচনা করেছি. The word নিয়ে (niye) carries the sense of “about,” so learners attach about to discuss.
band_9_corrections: I discussed the problem with my teacher.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Discuss is a transitive verb: it takes a direct object with no preposition after it. The same is true of enter, approach, reach, marry, request, and lack. You discuss a problem, not discuss about a problem. If you want a noun, use have a discussion about.
items.examiner_insight: This single preposition is one of the most reliable markers of a Bangladeshi script. It falls under both Grammatical Range and Accuracy and Lexical Resource, because it is a collocation error. One instance is a slip; repeated instances signal a fossilised habit and hold you at Band 6.5.

items.incorrect_sentence: The writer emphasised on the need for reform.
items.bangla_logic: লেখক সংস্কারের প্রয়োজনীয়তার উপর জোর দিয়েছেন. জোর দেওয়া (jor deoa, “to give stress”) pairs with উপর (upor, “on”), so on is carried across.
band_9_corrections: The writer emphasised the need for reform.
The writer placed emphasis on the need for reform.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Emphasise is transitive and takes no preposition. The preposition on belongs only to the noun form: place emphasis on, put stress on. Choose one structure; do not mix them.
items.examiner_insight: This appears constantly in Task 2 essays about what a text or a policy “highlights.” Getting it right shows the examiner you control the verb and noun forms of the same idea, which is exactly the flexibility Band 7 rewards.

items.incorrect_sentence: We reached to the station just before the train left.
items.bangla_logic: আমরা স্টেশনে পৌঁছেছি. The locative ending ে (-e, “to/at”) on স্টেশন becomes to in English.
band_9_corrections: We reached the station just before the train left.
We arrived at the station just in time.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Reach is transitive: reach a place, no preposition. If you prefer arrive, it takes at (a point) or in (a large area): arrive at the station, arrive in Dhaka.
items.examiner_insight: Reach to is a small error but a frequent one in Speaking Part 2 narratives. Fixing it removes a recurring accuracy penalty from your storytelling.

items.incorrect_sentence: My cousin is married with a doctor.
items.bangla_logic: আমার চাচাতো ভাইয়ের একজন ডাক্তারের সাথে বিয়ে হয়েছে. সাথে (shathe) means “with,” so with follows married.
band_9_corrections: My cousin is married to a doctor.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: The fixed collocation is married to, never married with. You do something with another person, but you are married to them. Compare engaged to, related to.
items.examiner_insight: Relationship vocabulary comes up in Speaking Part 1 (family) constantly. A collocation slip here is minor in isolation but memorable to an examiner listening for natural word partnerships.

items.incorrect_sentence: My manager is senior than me.
items.bangla_logic: আমার ম্যানেজার আমার থেকে সিনিয়র. থেকে (theke) means both “from” and “than,” so learners use than after senior.
band_9_corrections: My manager is senior to me.
My manager is more experienced than I am.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: A small group of comparative adjectives from Latin take to, not than: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, prior to. Only ordinary comparatives (bigger, faster) take than.
items.examiner_insight: Using superior to and prior to correctly is a quiet Band 7.5 signal. It shows awareness of less common lexical items and their collocations, which the band descriptors reward directly.

items.incorrect_sentence: I prefer reading books than watching television.
items.bangla_logic: আমি টেলিভিশন দেখার থেকে বই পড়া বেশি পছন্দ করি. Again থেকে (theke, “than/from”) pulls in than.
band_9_corrections: I prefer reading books to watching television.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Prefer takes to, not than: prefer A to B. When both options are verbs, keep them in the same form: prefer reading to watching. The alternative structure is would rather read than watch, where than is correct.
items.examiner_insight: Prefer is a very high-frequency Speaking Part 1 verb. The prefer to pattern is one of the most cost-effective fixes in this chapter, because you will use it in almost every interview.
items.source_text: Error 6 · “I prefer reading books than watching television.” Bangla logic. আমি টেলিভিশন দেখার থেকে বই পড়া বেশি পছন্দ করি. Again থেকে (theke, “than/from”) pulls in than. items.incorrect_sentence: She is very good in mathematics and physics.
items.bangla_logic: সে অঙ্ক আর পদার্থবিজ্ঞানে খুব ভালো. The locative ে (-e, “in”) on the subject names becomes in.
band_9_corrections: She is very good at mathematics and physics.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Skill adjectives take at: good at, skilled at, talented at, poor at. In is used only for a field as a whole in a different structure (a degree in physics).
items.examiner_insight: Describing abilities is unavoidable in Speaking Part 1 (study and work). Good at versus good in is a classic adjective-plus-preposition test, and consistent accuracy here lifts your collocation profile.

items.incorrect_sentence: My teacher gave me a very useful advice.
items.bangla_logic: আমার শিক্ষক আমাকে একটি খুব দরকারি উপদেশ দিয়েছেন. উপদেশ (upodesh, “advice”) is countable in Bangla, so একটি (ekti, “a/one”) is attached.
band_9_corrections: My teacher gave me a very useful piece of advice.
My teacher gave me some very useful advice.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Advice is uncountable: no a/an, no plural -s, and a singular verb. To count it, use a partitive: a piece of advice, two pieces of advice.
items.examiner_insight: Uncountable-noun control is on the South Asian error checklist for a reason. Writing a advice or advices is an immediate Band 6 word-formation marker; the piece of fix signals you know the rule.
items.source_text: Error 8 · “My teacher gave me a very useful advice.” Bangla logic. আমার শিক্ষক আমাকে একটি খুব দরকারি উপদেশ দিয়েছেন. উপদেশ (upodesh, “advice”) is countable in Bangla, so একটি (ekti, “a/one”) is attached. items.incorrect_sentence: The library provides many informations and equipments.
items.bangla_logic: লাইব্রেরি অনেক তথ্য এবং সরঞ্জাম সরবরাহ করে. তথ্য (tottho) and সরঞ্জাম (shoronjam) behave as countable in Bangla, so the English plural -s is added.
band_9_corrections: The library provides a great deal of information and equipment.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Information, equipment, furniture, research, knowledge, accommodation, traffic, and progress are all uncountable in English. They never take -s. Quantify them with a great deal of, a large amount of, or much.
items.examiner_insight: These eight words appear in almost every academic essay. Pluralising even one of them repeatedly is enough to pull Lexical Resource down to Band 6, because word formation is scored inside that criterion.
items.source_text: Error 9 · “The library provides many informations and equipments.” Bangla logic. লাইব্রেরি অনেক তথ্য এবং সরঞ্জাম সরবরাহ করে. তথ্য (tottho) and সরঞ্জাম (shoronjam) behave as countable in Bangla, so the English plural -s is added. items.incorrect_sentence: I am completely agree with this statement.
items.bangla_logic: আমি এই বক্তব্যের সাথে সম্পূর্ণ একমত. একমত (ekmot) is a state of being “in agreement,” which feels like an adjective, so learners add am.
band_9_corrections: I completely agree with this statement.
I am in complete agreement with this statement.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Agree is a full verb, not an adjective. It does not take am/is/are. Either use the verb (I agree) or the noun phrase (I am in agreement). Never am agree.
items.examiner_insight: Agree-and-disagree essays are the most common Task 2 type. Opening with I am agree in the first sentence signals a Band 5.5 grammar profile before the examiner has read your argument. This is a high-value fix.
items.source_text: Error 10 · “I am completely agree with this statement.” Bangla logic. আমি এই বক্তব্যের সাথে সম্পূর্ণ একমত. একমত (ekmot) is a state of being “in agreement,” which feels like an adjective, so learners add am. items.incorrect_sentence: Everybody in my office are working overtime this week.
items.bangla_logic: আমার অফিসের সবাই এই সপ্তাহে অতিরিক্ত সময় কাজ করছে. সবাই (shobai, “everybody”) refers to many people, so the verb feels plural.
band_9_corrections: Everybody in my office is working overtime this week.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Everybody, everyone, somebody, nobody, each, and neither are grammatically singular and take a singular verb, however many people they describe. The interrupting phrase (in my office) does not change this.
items.examiner_insight: Subject-verb agreement with indefinite pronouns is a frequent Band 6 slip. Because it recurs across a whole script, a single fixed habit here protects marks in every paragraph.

items.incorrect_sentence: One of my friend is studying in Canada.
items.bangla_logic: আমার এক বন্ধু কানাডায় পড় ছে. এক বন্ধু (ek bondhu, “one friend”) is singular in Bangla, so friend stays singular.
band_9_corrections: One of my friends is studying in Canada.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: After one of, the noun must be plural (one of my friends), because you are selecting one from a group. The verb, however, stays singular because the true subject is one: one of my friends is.
items.examiner_insight: This is a two-part trap: plural noun, singular verb. Candidates usually fix one half and miss the other. Getting both right is a clear Band 7 accuracy signal in Speaking Part 1.
items.source_text: Error 12 · “One of my friend is studying in Canada.” Bangla logic. আমার এক বন্ধু কানাডায় পড় ছে. এক বন্ধু (ek bondhu, “one friend”) is singular in Bangla, so friend stays singular. items.incorrect_sentence: Every students must bring their identity card.
items.bangla_logic: প্রত্যেক ছাত্রকে তাদের পরিচয়পত্র আনতে হবে. Bangla nouns are not forced into a plural form, so ছাত্র (chhatro, “student”) is read as flexible.
band_9_corrections: Every student must bring their identity card.
All students must bring their identity cards.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Every and each are always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: every student is. If you want a plural noun, switch the determiner to all: all students are.
items.examiner_insight: Every plus a plural noun is a basic countability error that caps Grammatical Range and Accuracy quickly. The fix is mechanical once you pair every with singular in your mind.
items.source_text: Error 13 · “Every students must bring their identity card.” Bangla logic. প্রত্যেক ছাত্রকে তাদের পরিচয়পত্র আনতে হবে. items.incorrect_sentence: The number of road accidents are increasing every year.
items.bangla_logic: সড় ক দুর্ঘটনার সংখ্যা প্রতি বছর বাড় ছে. The plural idea “accidents” sits right before the verb and pulls it toward plural.
band_9_corrections: The number of road accidents is increasing every year.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: The subject of this sentence is number (singular), not accidents. The number of + plural noun takes a singular verb. Contrast a number of + plural noun, which means “several” and takes a plural verb: a number of accidents are unreported.
items.examiner_insight: This exact phrase, the number of, is a Task 1 workhorse. Getting the agreement right on it is one of the most visible accuracy wins available in a data description.
items.source_text: Error 14 · “The number of road accidents are increasing every year.” Bangla logic. সড় ক দুর্ঘটনার সংখ্যা প্রতি বছর বাড় ছে. items.incorrect_sentence: Despite of the heavy rain, the ceremony continued.
items.bangla_logic: ভারী বৃষ্টি সত্ত্বেও, অনুষ্ঠান চলতে থাকল. সত্ত্বেও (sotteo) translates as “in spite of,” so learners blend the two and produce despite of.
band_9_corrections: Despite the heavy rain, the ceremony continued.
In spite of the heavy rain, the ceremony continued.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Despite takes no of. In spite of keeps its of. Both are followed by a noun or an -ing form, never a full clause. For a full clause, use although: Although it rained heavily, the ceremony continued.
items.examiner_insight: The despite of blend is one of the single most common concession errors in Bangladeshi Task 2 writing. Because concession is a core essay move, this error surfaces often and is worth eliminating completely.
items.source_text: Error 15 · “Despite of the heavy rain, the ceremony continued.” Bangla logic. ভারী বৃষ্টি সত্ত্বেও, অনুষ্ঠান চলতে থাকল. সত্ত্বেও (sotteo) translates as “in spite of,” so learners blend the two and produce despite of. items.incorrect_sentence: After his studies, he returned back to his hometown.
items.bangla_logic: পড়াশোনা শেষে সে তার নিজ শহরে ফিরে গেছে. ফিরে যাওয়া (phire jaoa) already contains the sense of “returning back,” so back is added on top in English.
band_9_corrections: After his studies, he returned to his hometown.
items.grammar_lexical_rule: Return already means “go back,” so returned back is redundant. The same redundancy affects repeat again, revert back, reverse back, and ascend up. Use the single verb.
items.examiner_insight: Redundancy is a Lexical Resource weakness: it shows the meaning of a word has not been fully absorbed. Trimming these doublings makes your writing tighter and more precise, which is exactly the Band 8 quality of “conveying precise meaning.”

items.incorrect_sentence: My friend told to me that the interview went well.

items.incorrect_sentence: Maximum people in my country depend on agriculture.

items.incorrect_sentence: I have not met my school friends since a long time.

আমি ২০১৮ সাল থেকে এই বিষয়ের উপর গবেষণা করছি।
দূষণ জনস্বাস্থ্যের জন্য একটি মারাত্মক হুমকি সৃষ্টি করছে।
তরুণ প্রজন্মের জন্য কর্মসংস্থানের সুযোগ তৈরি করা অত্যন্ত জরুরি।
যদিও অনেক শিক্ষার্থী ইংরেজিতে ভালো, তবুও তারা পরীক্ষায় ভালো ফল করতে পারে না।
আমি একদিন আমার নিজের একটি প্রতিষ্ঠান গড়ে তুলতে চাই।
দারিদ্র্য দূর করা যেকোনো উন্নয়নশীল দেশের সবচেয়ে বড় চ্যালেঞ্জ।
যদি সরকার আরও কঠোর আইন প্রণয়ন করত, তাহলে অপরাধের হার কমে যেত।

blocks.source_text: Exercise 1.2 · Bangla to Band 9 Translation Challenge Read each Bangla thought and write one natural, error-free IELTS sentence that expresses it. Do not translate word by word; translate the meaning. Each thought hides at least one of the traps from Part A. 1. বেশিরভাগ মানুষ মনে করে যে প্রযুক্তি আমাদের দৈনন্দিন জীবনকে অনেক সহজ করেছে। 2. যানজট সত্ত্বেও, শহরের বেশিরভাগ মানুষ এখনও ব্যক্তিগত গাড়ি ব্যবহার করতে পছন্দ করে। 3. আমার মতে, সরকারের উচিত শিক্ষা খাতে আরও বেশি বিনিয়োগ করা। 4. আমি ২০১৮ সাল থেকে এই বিষয়ের উপর গবেষণা করছি। 5. দূষণ জনস্বাস্থ্যের জন্য একটি মারাত্মক হুমকি সৃষ্টি করছে। 6. তরুণ প্রজন্মের জন্য কর্মসংস্থানের সুযোগ তৈরি করা অত্যন্ত জরুরি। 7. যদিও অনেক শিক্ষার্থী ইংরেজিতে ভালো, তবুও তারা পরীক্ষায় ভালো ফল করতে পারে না। 8. আমি একদিন আমার নিজের একটি প্রতিষ্ঠান গড়ে তুলতে চাই। 9. দারিদ্র্য দূর করা যেকোনো উন্নয়নশীল দেশের সবচেয়ে বড় চ্যালেঞ্জ। 10. যদি সরকার আরও কঠোর আইন প্রণয়ন করত, তাহলে অপরাধের হার কমে যেত।

source_text: Chapter 1: The Bangladeshi L1 Interference Fixer Most Bangladeshi candidates lose their easiest marks here. The sentences in this chapter are not produced by weak students. They are produced by strong, fluent students whose English is being quietly shaped by Bangla underneath. Each error below is a faithful translation of a perfectly correct Bangla thought. The Bangla is not the problem. The word-for-word carrying of Bangla structure into English is the problem, and an examiner recognises it instantly. This is called first-language (L1) interference. It is predictable, it is patterned, and because it is patterned, it is fixable. Work through all thirty errors and note which ones you produce yourself. Then do the two exercise sets at the end with a pen before checking the key. Each entry gives you five things: the incorrect sentence, the Bangla logic that produces it, the Band 9 correction, the precise grammar or lexical rule, and the examiner’s view of what it costs you. Part A: The 30 Core Errors Error 1 · “I discussed about the problem with my teacher.” Bangla logic. আমি শিক্ষকের সাথে সমস্যাটি নিয়ে আলোচনা করেছি. The word নিয়ে (niye) carries the sense of “about,” so learners attach about to discuss. Band 9 correction. I discussed the problem with my teacher. Grammar and lexical rule. Discuss is a transitive verb: it takes a direct object with no preposition after it. The same is true of enter, approach, reach, marry, request, and lack. You discuss a problem, not discuss about a problem. If you want a noun, use have a discussion about. Examiner insight. This single preposition is one of the most reliable markers of a Bangladeshi script. It falls under both Grammatical Range and Accuracy and Lexical Resource, because it is a collocation error. One instance is a slip; repeated instances signal a fossilised habit and hold you at Band 6.5. Error 2 · “The writer emphasised on the need for reform.” Bangla logic. লেখক সংস্কারের প্রয়োজনীয়তার উপর জোর দিয়েছেন. জোর দেওয়া (jor deoa, “to give stress”) pairs with উপর (upor, “on”), so on is carried across. Band 9 correction. The writer emphasised the need for reform. / The writer placed emphasis on the need for reform. Grammar and lexical rule. Emphasise is transitive and takes no preposition. The preposition on belongs only to the noun form: place emphasis on, put stress on. Choose one structure; do not mix them. Examiner insight. This appears constantly in Task 2 essays about what a text or a policy “highlights.” Getting it right shows the examiner you control the verb and noun forms of the same idea, which is exactly the flexibility Band 7 rewards. Error 3 · “We reached to the station just before the train left.” Bangla logic. আমরা স্টেশনে পৌঁছেছি. The locative ending ে (-e, “to/at”) on স্টেশন becomes to in English. Band 9 correction. We reached the station just before the train left. / We arrived at the station just in time. Grammar and lexical rule. Reach is transitive: reach a place, no preposition. If you prefer arrive, it takes at (a point) or in (a large area): arrive at the station, arrive in Dhaka. Examiner insight. Reach to is a small error but a frequent one in Speaking Part 2 narratives. Fixing it removes a recurring accuracy penalty from your storytelling. Error 4 · “My cousin is married with a doctor.” Bangla logic. আমার চাচাতো ভাইয়ের একজন ডাক্তারের সাথে বিয়ে হয়েছে. সাথে (shathe) means “with,” so with follows married. Band 9 correction. My cousin is married to a doctor. Grammar and lexical rule. The fixed collocation is married to, never married with. You do something with another person, but you are married to them. Compare engaged to, related to. Examiner insight. Relationship vocabulary comes up in Speaking Part 1 (family) constantly. A collocation slip here is minor in isolation but memorable to an examiner listening for natural word partnerships. Error 5 · “My manager is senior than me.” Bangla logic. আমার ম্যানেজার আমার থেকে সিনিয়র. থেকে (theke) means both “from” and “than,” so learners use than after senior. Band 9 correction. My manager is senior to me. / My manager is more experienced than I am. Grammar and lexical rule. A small group of comparative adjectives from Latin take to, not than: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, prior to. Only ordinary comparatives (bigger, faster) take than. Examiner insight. Using superior to and prior to correctly is a quiet Band 7.5 signal. It shows awareness of less common lexical items and their collocations, which the band descriptors reward directly. Error 6 · “I prefer reading books than watching television.” Bangla logic. আমি টেলিভিশন দেখার থেকে বই পড়া বেশি পছন্দ করি. Again থেকে (theke, “than/from”) pulls in than. Band 9 correction. I prefer reading books to watching television. Grammar and lexical rule. Prefer takes to, not than: prefer A to B. When both options are verbs, keep them in the same form: prefer reading to watching. The alternative structure is would rather read than watch, where than is correct. Examiner insight. Prefer is a very high-frequency Speaking Part 1 verb. The prefer to pattern is one of the most cost-effective fixes in this chapter, because you will use it in almost every interview. Error 7 · “She is very good in mathematics and physics.” Bangla logic. সে অঙ্ক আর পদার্থবিজ্ঞানে খুব ভালো. The locative ে (-e, “in”) on the subject names becomes in. Band 9 correction. She is very good at mathematics and physics. Grammar and lexical rule. Skill adjectives take at: good at, skilled at, talented at, poor at. In is used only for a field as a whole in a different structure (a degree in physics). Examiner insight. Describing abilities is unavoidable in Speaking Part 1 (study and work). Good at versus good in is a classic adjective-plus-preposition test, and consistent accuracy here lifts your collocation profile. Error 8 · “My teacher gave me a very useful advice.” Bangla logic. আমার শিক্ষক আমাকে একটি খুব দরকারি উপদেশ দিয়েছেন. উপদেশ (upodesh, “advice”) is countable in Bangla, so একটি (ekti, “a/one”) is attached. Band 9 correction. My teacher gave me a very useful piece of advice. / My teacher gave me some very useful advice. Grammar and lexical rule. Advice is uncountable: no a/an, no plural -s, and a singular verb. To count it, use a partitive: a piece of advice, two pieces of advice. Examiner insight. Uncountable-noun control is on the South Asian error checklist for a reason. Writing a advice or advices is an immediate Band 6 word-formation marker; the piece of fix signals you know the rule. Error 9 · “The library provides many informations and equipments.” Bangla logic. লাইব্রেরি অনেক তথ্য এবং সরঞ্জাম সরবরাহ করে. তথ্য (tottho) and সরঞ্জাম (shoronjam) behave as countable in Bangla, so the English plural -s is added. Band 9 correction. The library provides a great deal of information and equipment. Grammar and lexical rule. Information, equipment, furniture, research, knowledge, accommodation, traffic, and progress are all uncountable in English. They never take -s. Quantify them with a great deal of, a large amount of, or much. Examiner insight. These eight words appear in almost every academic essay. Pluralising even one of them repeatedly is enough to pull Lexical Resource down to Band 6, because word formation is scored inside that criterion. Error 10 · “I am completely agree with this statement.” Bangla logic. আমি এই বক্তব্যের সাথে সম্পূর্ণ একমত. একমত (ekmot) is a state of being “in agreement,” which feels like an adjective, so learners add am. Band 9 correction. I completely agree with this statement. / I am in complete agreement with this statement. Grammar and lexical rule. Agree is a full verb, not an adjective. It does not take am/is/are. Either use the verb (I agree) or the noun phrase (I am in agreement). Never am agree. Examiner insight. Agree-and-disagree essays are the most common Task 2 type. Opening with I am agree in the first sentence signals a Band 5.5 grammar profile before the examiner has read your argument. This is a high-value fix. Error 11 · “Everybody in my office are working overtime this week.” Bangla logic. আমার অফিসের সবাই এই সপ্তাহে অতিরিক্ত সময় কাজ করছে. সবাই (shobai, “everybody”) refers to many people, so the verb feels plural. Band 9 correction. Everybody in my office is working overtime this week. Grammar and lexical rule. Everybody, everyone, somebody, nobody, each, and neither are grammatically singular and take a singular verb, however many people they describe. The interrupting phrase (in my office) does not change this. Examiner insight. Subject-verb agreement with indefinite pronouns is a frequent Band 6 slip. Because it recurs across a whole script, a single fixed habit here protects marks in every paragraph. Error 12 · “One of my friend is studying in Canada.” Bangla logic. আমার এক বন্ধু কানাডায় পড় ছে. এক বন্ধু (ek bondhu, “one friend”) is singular in Bangla, so friend stays singular. Band 9 correction. One of my friends is studying in Canada. Grammar and lexical rule. After one of, the noun must be plural (one of my friends), because you are selecting one from a group. The verb, however, stays singular because the true subject is one: one of my friends is. Examiner insight. This is a two-part trap: plural noun, singular verb. Candidates usually fix one half and miss the other. Getting both right is a clear Band 7 accuracy signal in Speaking Part 1. Error 13 · “Every students must bring their identity card.” Bangla logic. প্রত্যেক ছাত্রকে তাদের পরিচয়পত্র আনতে হবে. Bangla nouns are not forced into a plural form, so ছাত্র (chhatro, “student”) is read as flexible. Band 9 correction. Every student must bring their identity card. / All students must bring their identity cards. Grammar and lexical rule. Every and each are always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb: every student is. If you want a plural noun, switch the determiner to all: all students are. Examiner insight. Every plus a plural noun is a basic countability error that caps Grammatical Range and Accuracy quickly. The fix is mechanical once you pair every with singular in your mind. Error 14 · “The number of road accidents are increasing every year.” Bangla logic. সড় ক দুর্ঘটনার সংখ্যা প্রতি বছর বাড় ছে. The plural idea “accidents” sits right before the verb and pulls it toward plural. Band 9 correction. The number of road accidents is increasing every year. Grammar and lexical rule. The subject of this sentence is number (singular), not accidents. The number of + plural noun takes a singular verb. Contrast a number of + plural noun, which means “several” and takes a plural verb: a number of accidents are unreported. Examiner insight. This exact phrase, the number of, is a Task 1 workhorse. Getting the agreement right on it is one of the most visible accuracy wins available in a data description. Error 15 · “Despite of the heavy rain, the ceremony continued.” Bangla logic. ভারী বৃষ্টি সত্ত্বেও, অনুষ্ঠান চলতে থাকল. সত্ত্বেও (sotteo) translates as “in spite of,” so learners blend the two and produce despite of. Band 9 correction. Despite the heavy rain, the ceremony continued. / In spite of the heavy rain, the ceremony continued. Grammar and lexical rule. Despite takes no of. In spite of keeps its of. Both are followed by a noun or an -ing form, never a full clause. For a full clause, use although: Although it rained heavily, the ceremony continued. Examiner insight. The despite of blend is one of the single most common concession errors in Bangladeshi Task 2 writing. Because concession is a core essay move, this error surfaces often and is worth eliminating completely. Error 16 · “After his studies, he returned back to his hometown.” Bangla logic. পড়াশোনা শেষে সে তার নিজ শহরে ফিরে গেছে. ফিরে যাওয়া (phire jaoa) already contains the sense of “returning back,” so back is added on top in English. Band 9 correction. After his studies, he returned to his hometown. Grammar and lexical rule. Return already means “go back,” so returned back is redundant. The same redundancy affects repeat again, revert back, reverse back, and ascend up. Use the single verb. Examiner insight. Redundancy is a Lexical Resource weakness: it shows the meaning of a word has not been fully absorbed. Trimming these doublings makes your writing tighter and more precise, which is exactly the Band 8 quality of “conveying precise meaning.” Error 17 · “Students must learn to cope up with academic pressure.” Bangla logic. শিক্ষার্থীদের শিক্ষাগত চাপের সাথে খাপ খাওয়াতে শিখতে হবে. There is no up in the Bangla; the up is added by false analogy with other phrasal verbs like keep up, put up with. Band 9 correction. Students must learn to cope with academic pressure. Grammar and lexical rule. The verb is cope with, with no up. The intruding up is a South Asian regional habit. Compare the correct put up with (tolerate), which is a genuinely different phrasal verb. Examiner insight. Phrasal-verb accuracy is scored under Lexical Resource. Cope up with is instantly recognisable to examiners as a regional error, so removing it sharpens the natural, native quality your Speaking band depends on. Error 18 · “The committee comprises of twelve senior members.” Bangla logic. কমিটি বারো জন প্রবীণ সদস্য নিয়ে গঠিত. নিয়ে গঠিত (niye gothito, “formed with/of”) maps to “comprises of.” Band 9 correction. The committee comprises twelve senior members. / The committee is composed of twelve senior members. / The committee consists of twelve senior members. Grammar and lexical rule. Comprise is transitive and takes no of. The of belongs to consist of and be composed of. Never mix them into comprises of. Examiner insight. This is a favourite in Task 1 pie-chart and process descriptions. Choosing consists of or comprises correctly shows control of a less common academic verb, a Band 7 range marker. Error 19 · “I have visited Cox’s Bazar last winter with my family.” Bangla logic. আমি গত শীতে পরিবারসহ কক্সবাজার গিয়েছি. Conversational Bangla uses one past form for both “I went” and “I have gone,” so the present perfect is over-applied. Band 9 correction. I visited Cox’s Bazar last winter with my family. Grammar and lexical rule. A finished time expression (last winter, in 2019, two years ago) forces the simple past. The present perfect cannot appear with a stated finished time. Use present perfect only for open or continuing time (I have visited Cox’s Bazar several times). Examiner insight. This tense clash is a content-level error in Speaking Part 2, where you narrate a past experience. Consistent past tense across a two-minute talk is a strong fluency and accuracy signal. Error 20 · “I am living in Dhaka since 2015.” Bangla logic. আমি ২০১৫ সাল থেকে ঢাকায় থাকছি. The Bangla continuous থাকছি (thakchhi) covers ongoing duration, so it maps to the English present continuous. Band 9 correction. I have been living in Dhaka since 2015. / I have lived in Dhaka since 2015. Grammar and lexical rule. A duration that started in the past and continues now needs the present perfect or present perfect continuous, not the present continuous. The signal words since and for pull you toward the perfect form. Examiner insight. Time-frame control separates Band 6 from Band 7 in Speaking Part 1. The have been + -ing since pattern is a high-frequency structure worth drilling until it is automatic. Error 21 · “My friend told to me that the interview went well.” Bangla logic. আমার বন্ধু আমাকে বলল যে সাক্ষাৎকারটি ভালো হয়েছে. আমাকে বলল (amake bollo, “told me”) includes a “to me” sense that gets spelled out in English. Band 9 correction. My friend told me that the interview went well. / My friend said to me that the interview went well. Grammar and lexical rule. Tell takes a person directly with no to (tell me, tell him). Say needs to before a person (say to me). The two verbs pattern differently: tell someone something versus say something to someone. Examiner insight. Reported speech runs through Speaking Part 2 narratives. The tell/say split is a precise lexical distinction, and controlling it reads as genuine command of high-frequency reporting verbs. Error 22 · “According to me, the voting age should be lowered.” Bangla logic. আমার মতে, ভোটের বয়স কমানো উচিত. আমার মতে (amar mote) is a fixed phrase for “in my opinion,” and it maps too literally onto “according to me.” Band 9 correction. In my opinion, the voting age should be lowered. / To my mind, the voting age should be lowered. Grammar and lexical rule. According to introduces an external source (according to the report, according to experts), not your own view. For your own view, use in my opinion, from my perspective, or I would argue that. Examiner insight. According to me is one of the most frequent opinion-phrase errors in Bangladeshi Task 2 essays and Speaking Part 3. Replacing it with a varied set of opinion markers lifts both Lexical Resource and the academic register examiners expect. Error 23 · “Maximum people in my country depend on agriculture.” Bangla logic. আমার দেশের বেশিরভাগ মানুষ কৃ ষির উপর নির্ভর করে. বেশিরভাগ (beshirbhag, “most”) is mistranslated as “maximum.” Band 9 correction. Most people in my country depend on agriculture. / The majority of people in my country depend on agriculture. Grammar and lexical rule. Maximum is a noun or adjective meaning the highest possible amount (the maximum speed). It does not mean “most.” For the greater part of a group, use most, the majority of, or the bulk of. Examiner insight. Maximum people is a clear word-choice error under Lexical Resource. Swapping it for the majority of or the bulk of also gives you the range of quantifiers that Task 2 rewards. Error 24 · “I have to give an important exam at the end of this month.” Bangla logic. এই মাসের শেষে আমাকে একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পরীক্ষা দিতে হবে. পরীক্ষা দেওয়া (porikkha deoa, “to give an exam”) uses দেওয়া (deoa, “give”), so learners say “give an exam.” Band 9 correction. I have to sit an important exam at the end of this month. / I have to take an important exam at the end of this month. Grammar and lexical rule. In English, a student sits or takes an exam; only the examiner or institution sets or gives one. Give an exam reverses the roles. Examiner insight. Education vocabulary is central to Speaking Part 1. Sit an exam (British usage, favoured in IELTS) is a natural collocation that immediately reads as more native than give an exam. Error 25 · “Try not to do the same mistake in the next test.” Bangla logic. পরের পরীক্ষায় একই ভু ল কোরো না. ভু ল করা (bhul kora) uses করা (kora), which covers both “do” and “make,” so do a mistake results. Band 9 correction. Try not to make the same mistake in the next test. Grammar and lexical rule. English splits do and make by collocation. You make a mistake, a decision, progress, an effort, an arrangement; you do homework, research, a favour, business, damage. Bangla করা covers all of these, so the split must be learned as fixed pairs. Examiner insight. The do/make division is one of the highest-frequency collocation tests in the language. Consistent accuracy is a strong Lexical Resource signal; frequent slips cap you at Band 6. Error 26 · “I have not met my school friends since a long time.” Bangla logic. আমি অনেকদিন ধরে আমার স্কু লের বন্ধু দের সাথে দেখা করিনি. ধরে (dhore) marks a stretch of time and is loosely read as “since.” Band 9 correction. I have not met my school friends for a long time. Grammar and lexical rule. Since is followed by a point in time when something began (since 2015, since Monday). For is followed by a length of time (for a long time, for three years). “A long time” is a duration, so it takes for. Examiner insight. The since/for distinction pairs directly with the present perfect from Error 20. Mastering both together removes a cluster of related errors that otherwise recur throughout Speaking Part 1. Error 27 · “Please off the fan and light before you leave the room.” Bangla logic. ঘর ছাড়ার আগে ফ্যান আর লাইট বন্ধ করো. বন্ধ করা (bondho kora, “to close/shut off”) becomes “off,” and খোলা (khola, “to open”) becomes “open,” giving off the fan, open the light. Band 9 correction. Please turn off the fan and the light before you leave the room. Grammar and lexical rule. English uses the phrasal verbs turn on and turn off (or switch on/off) for electrical devices. Off is not a verb, and open/close apply to doors and windows, not to lights and fans. Examiner insight. Open the light and off the fan are unmistakable regional calques. They rarely appear in Writing but surface in Speaking Part 1 about home and daily routine, where natural phrasal verbs are exactly what the examiner is listening for. Error 28 · “My all relatives gathered for the wedding celebration.” Bangla logic. আমার সব আত্মীয় বিয়ের অনুষ্ঠানে জড়ো হয়েছিল. আমার সব (amar shob, literally “my all”) places the possessive before all, and the order carries over. Band 9 correction. All my relatives gathered for the wedding celebration. Grammar and lexical rule. In English, all comes before the possessive: all my relatives, all his money, all our efforts. The Bangla order “my all” is reversed. The same holds for both my parents, half my salary. Examiner insight. Determiner order is a subtle Grammatical Range and Accuracy point. It is minor in isolation but, when consistent, contributes to the smooth, natural flow that distinguishes higher-band speech and writing. Error 29 · “Myself Rahim, and I am here to talk about my hometown.” Bangla logic. আমি রহিম, আর আমি আমার শহর নিয়ে কথা বলতে এসেছি. The self-introduction habit of announcing oneself becomes the non-standard “Myself Rahim.” Band 9 correction. My name is Rahim, and I am here to talk about my hometown. / I am Rahim, and I would like to talk about my hometown. Grammar and lexical rule. Myself is a reflexive pronoun (I did it myself); it cannot introduce a name. Use My name is or I am followed by the name. Examiner insight. In the IELTS Speaking test you are not required to introduce yourself formally, but if you do, Myself Rahim is an instant regional marker. The natural I am Rahim sets a stronger first impression on fluency and lexis. Error 30 · “I passed out from university in 2019 with a degree in economics.” Bangla logic. This is an institutional-English habit rather than a direct Bangla translation: “pass out” is widely used across South Asia to mean “graduate.” Band 9 correction. I graduated from university in 2019 with a degree in economics. Grammar and lexical rule. In standard English, pass out means to faint or lose consciousness. To complete a degree, use graduate from or complete my studies at. This is a false friend, not a grammar error. Examiner insight. Passed out from university can genuinely confuse an examiner, because the standard meaning is “fainted.” Since education background is asked in almost every Speaking Part 1, replacing it with graduated from protects clarity and register at the same time.
